message.reasoning_content:
=Planning complete.=

I'll analyze the current solution and propose a Tier 2/3 improvement plan focused on the plateau.

Current state: the pipeline is a 3-way ensemble (NN with embeddings + HistGB with native categoricals + ExtraTrees) blended by an OOF-searched simplex weight vector, plus smoothing target encoding (TE) on identities and 5 hand-crafted interactions. Score plateaued at 0.7443. The blend is dominated by GBDT-family members with highly correlated feature views (all consume the same TE block and same numeric block), so gains from adding a third correlated member are marginal and the OOF weight search is likely overfitting the blend weights on ~8k rows (accuracy is a coarse, high-variance objective for weight search).

Tier 2 change (representation + component swap), two coupled moves:

1. Feature representation: replace the current TE block (which only captures marginal category-acceptance) with a richer, leakage-free representation: (a) keep TE, (b) ADD pairwise cross-feature counts + TE for a directed set of domain interactions (coupon×distance×time already partly there; extend with coupon×occupation, coupon×education, coupon×Bar/CoffeeHouse usage, time×temperature), and (c) add numeric aggregates such as coupon-acceptance prior distance (TE minus prior) and per-row "usage sum" and "coupon match to usage" features (e.g. does the customer's Bar frequency align with a Bar coupon). These match the domain intuition that coupon acceptance hinges on usage-habit alignment with the offered coupon type, which the raw frequency columns currently only encode separately.

2. Component change: replace the ExtraTrees member (weakest, highly correlated with HistGB) with a differently-biased learner: a second GBDT family member with a different objective/parameterization — specifically a LightGBM-style leaf-wise model if available, otherwise a CatBoost-like ordered-target model is not installed; fall back to a deep, high-cardinality-aware HistGB variant plus a RandomForest — but more reliably, replace ET with a calibrated k-NN / MLP over the engineered interaction features won't help either.

The most defensible Tier 2 move: keep the NN and GBDT but fix the blend overfitting by replacing the OOF accuracy simplex search with a regularized blend (weight shrinkage + probability calibration via temperature scaling fitted on OOF), and simultaneously add the coupon-usage-alignment features. This keeps the paradigm but materially changes the representation and the combination rule.

Concretely, three component changes:

A. data_processing_and_feature_engineering: add coupon-usage-alignment features (5 features: for each frequency column, feature = usage_level if the offered coupon corresponds to that venue else 0/NaN-aware baseline), plus coupon-specific TE and two extra interactions (coupon×occupation, coupon×income already present, add coupon×education and coupon×temperature-bucket), all fitted only on training rows with the existing fold-safe machinery.

B. model_design: replace ExtraTrees with a genuinely decorrelated member — a calibrated sklearn MLPClassifier on the ET one-hot+TE matrix, OR better, a second NN with a different architecture (wider embeddings, 3 layers, higher dropout) sharing the same features but different inductive bias. Two NNs with different widths/deptand a GBDT give three genuinely different error patterns; ET was redundant with HistGB.

C. training_evaluation: replace the unregularized OOF simplex accuracy search with a shrunk/regularized blend: average the OOF-optimal weights with uniform weights (shrinkage λ=0.5) and select via a repeated stratified K-fold split of OOF rows to estimate blend accuracy (reduces weight overfitting); also add temperature scaling per component before blending, fitted on OOF log-loss. This is the piece most likely to explain why OOF blend acc (probably ~0.75) does not transfer to the 0.7443 supervisor score.

Why this addresses the plateau root cause: the current members all see nearly the same TE+numeric view, so blending them cannot reduce variance beyond the best single member; the plateau reflects limited representation (marginal TE only) and a blend-selection procedure that inflates OOF accuracy. Adding usage-alignment features injects the missing domain signal (does the customer actually use this coupon type), and diversification + regularized blending converts that signal into held-out accuracy instead of OOF overfit.

I will implement exactly this: add the alignment/interaction features (A) and the regularized blend with a second, differently-shaped NN member (B+C), leaving the leakage-safe fold machinery intact.
